1609_2024.shift_or_short_column: The 2024 table is a transposition, not a shift: each printed row of the 2024 table equals one UW-year column of the 2023 report's table, with one new cell appended at the end-2024 age (the 2023 report has no row longer than 3, the 2024 one has 4). wording.represented: p14, 'Representation of notes to the Accounts': "The notes to the accounts have been represented to align to the Corporation of Lloyds mandated disclosure. Unless otherwise stated there is no restatement of any figures." This is a statement of a change of presentation with no restatement. A literal reading would restate UW2021 end-2023 by +49% and UW2023 first-year by -34% against the 2023 report with no explanation, which the sentence rules out. A layout change in which the triangle was turned on its side (rows = UW years) while the headings kept the old axes is what the sentence and the overlay jointly imply.
wording.pure_underwriting_year: p51 'Pure underwriting year' is the label of the left column of the table (the Lloyd's mandated heading for an underwriting-year basis table); it says the estimates are on a UW-year (ultimate, unearned included) basis, not which axis holds the years. It does not describe a reallocation between years; no wording of a reallocation between underwriting years appears in either filing (2024 text searched for 'restat', 'reallocat', 're-present', 'represented', 'pure underwriting year').
wording.paid_row_caveat: The printed 'Less gross claims paid' line has one value per printed column (11,286 | 48,102 | 3,698 | 3,931). Read by column heads these are UW 2021-2024 paid; if the body is transposed the paid line may be mis-bound too. It does not enter M and its total (67,017) is axis-independent, so the caveat does not change M or the reconciliation.

explanation.restatement_search: Searched 2016 and 2017 text for restat / re-present / reclassif / retranslat / correct / merge / 958 / RITC / reinsurance to close. No restatement, re-presentation or correction of the claims development table in either filing. The only restatements are of 2015 financial-instrument comparatives (2016 report: '2015 (restated)', fair value hierarchy and liability maturities).
explanation.stated_in_2017: p24: 'Historic development includes a mix of prior year releases and deteriorations, and in 2017 gross and net deteriorations occurred.' p5: 'A strengthening of prior period reserves' and 'The partial recovery of the value of Sterling against the US Dollar' as drivers of 2017.
explanation.syndicate_958: 2017 p5: 'With effect from the 2016 year of account, CMA merged Syndicate 958's capacity into Syndicate 4444. The 2015 year of account for Syndicate 958 will be reinsured to close into Syndicate 4444, effective from 1 January 2018.' 2017 p7 (future developments): 'At 31 December 2017, Syndicate 4444 accepted the reinsurance to close for the 2015 year of account of Syndicate 958, its final underwriting year.' The 2018 report settles the timing: p17 'With effect from 1 January 2018 the 2015 year of account for Syndicate 958 has been reinsured to close (RITC'd) into Syndicate 4444. The financial statements include the RITC of syndicate 958, 2017 comparatives for syndicate 4444 are pre the RITC.' So the RITC is not in the 2017 table or accounts (and p7's 'At 31 December 2017' wording is a signing date, not a recognition date). The 2016 merger of 958's capacity affects the 2016 year of account onward, not the 2011-2015 columns. Nothing in either filing links the RITC to the end-2016 history of the 2017 table.
explanation.fx: No exchange rate is printed. Direction from the filing: 2017 p5 lists 'the partial recovery of the value of Sterling against the US Dollar' (Sterling stronger: US dollar amounts become fewer pounds); US dollar technical provisions are 1,227,673 of 2,003,465 = 61% (2017 p31). The accounts' own translation effect on gross claims outstanding in 2017 is a reduction of 33,144 (balance sheet movement 346,658 less change in provision 379,802, p13/p16), 2.8% of the opening 1,200,561. So a stronger Sterling should lower the end-2016 cells in the 2017 table; they are 4.7% (2011, 2012) and 3.9% (2013) HIGHER and only 2014-2016 are within a few percent. In the control year the cells moved with the currency: the 2016 table's end-2015 cells are 2.3% to 10.7% higher than the 2015 print (2011 351,980 vs 344,242 = 1.0225; 2012 363,811 vs 351,920 = 1.0338; 2013 372,441 vs 356,540 = 1.0446; 2014 385,327 vs 360,033 = 1.0703; 2015 240,706 vs 217,535 = 1.1065), in a year the 2016 report describes as 'a fall in the value of Sterling against the US Dollar following the UK's decision to leave the European Union' (2016 p5). That is the direction an FX rise would give, and the size is plausible for the share of US dollar business. 2017 moves the other way in the old years, so currency does not explain it.

4444_2017.valid_case_against: The table ties exactly to claims outstanding at both year-ends; the 2017 text says 'in 2017 gross and net deteriorations occurred' and 'A strengthening of prior period reserves', so an adverse M is the expected sign; the RITC of Syndicate 958 is after the year. Against that: no filing explains why end-2016 cells in the 2017 table sit 4.7%/4.7%/3.9% above the 2016 print for 2011/2012/2013 in a year Sterling strengthened (which lowers US dollar amounts), and the year's flows do not tie (incurred +6.3% to +11.9%, paid +30.8%) while the same tests are within 1-6% in the control year.
